title: Defining Functions and return
content:
What problem does this solve?
When the same calculation appears in many places — healing, doubling a bonus, formatting a status line — copy-pasting code becomes fragile. A function packages a reusable action under a name.

Basic syntax
  def double(number):
      return number * 2

What actually happens
def creates a function and binds it to the name double. Calling double(5) assigns 5 to the parameter number, runs the body, and return sends a value back to the caller. You have already been calling print and append; now you define a name other code can call.

Critical distinction
  print(result)  — shows something to a human
  return result  — gives a value to other code

If you only print inside a function, callers cannot use the computed value in further calculations.

When this is useful
Use a function when a calculation or action will be needed more than once, or when another piece of code must receive the result.
concepts: Parameters receive argument values for one call
return sends a value to the caller; print only displays

examples.title: print vs return
examples.code:
def add(a, b):
    return a + b

total = add(2, 3)
print(total)
examples.explanation: add returns 5. The caller stores it in total, then prints it.

examples.title: Only printing leaves the caller empty
examples.code:
def add(a, b):
    print(a + b)

total = add(2, 3)
print(total)
examples.explanation: The function prints 5 for a human, but return is missing, so total is None.

common_mistakes: Using print instead of return, then wondering why total is None
Forgetting parentheses when calling: add 2, 3 is invalid

exercises.title: Write double()
exercises.prompt:
Create a function double(number) that returns twice the supplied number.
Do not hardcode a single answer — it must work for many inputs.
hints: Think about which keyword sends a value back from a function.
You need to use return with an expression involving number.
Return an expression that uses number, not a fixed integer.

exercises.title: print or return?
exercises.prompt:
You are writing heal(character_health, amount) used by combat code that must continue calculating after healing.
Should the function print the new health, or return it, if other code must use the updated value?
choices: Only print the new health inside heal
Return the new health so callers can use it
exercises.success_message: Right — other code can only keep calculating if heal returns the new health.
exercises.failure_message: Printed text is for humans. If later code must use the new health, the function needs to return that number.
hints: Ask whether another function needs the numeric result.
Printed text is for humans; returned values are for programs.
Choose the option that returns the new health.

exercises.title: Write heal()
exercises.prompt:
Write heal(health, amount) that returns the new health after adding amount.
Return the number so other code can use it. Do not hardcode a single answer.
hints: The function receives two numbers: the current health and how much to add.
Return an expression that uses both parameters.

exercises.title: Format a status line
exercises.prompt:
Write format_status(name, health) that returns a string like:
Mira has 42 HP

Use an f-string. Return the text; do not print it. It must work for many names and health values.
hints: This function should return a string, not print one.
An f-string can mix the name and health into one sentence.
Return an f-string that includes name and health inside braces.

tests.message: Return an f-string that includes name and health in braces.
